accepted_claims: A single fixed property P consists of K4-free graphs that become 3-colorable after deletion of at most one vertex; P is hereditary, extendable and closed under edge deletion.

For all finite input sizes without knowing n, a one-sided classical canonical tester uses O(epsilon^-6 log(1/epsilon)) vertex samples and O(epsilon^-12 log^2(1/epsilon)) adjacency queries; no polynomial running-time bound is claimed.

Along the explicit positive-rational sequence epsilon_d=K/(1152m), every unrestricted adaptive two-sided VDF tester with error at most 1/3 has worst-case total sample-plus-adjacency cost exp(Omega(log^2(1/epsilon_d))).
With queries restricted to sampled labels, the same superpolynomial bound holds for vertex samples even with free induced adjacency queries; this is separate from the unrestricted total-cost theorem.

The exact arbitrary-repair weighted identity, explicit Behrend/Ruzsa–Szemeredi host, parity coupling and unconditional BAD farness argument establish the separation without omitted computational artifacts.
A doubled six-vertex wheel proves directly that P is not blowup-avoidable, including arbitrary internal edges in blowup classes.
not_claimed: A sample-only lower bound with unlimited free arbitrary named adjacency queries.
Polynomial running time for the classical tester.
A separation for every single forbidden-subgraph property.
Novelty, priority, external peer review or exhaustive current-literature clearance.
